verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's own docs show a few group-level operations: Node Pools apply one configuration to any number of Nodes and scale as a unit, bucket lifecycle policies apply actions like Expiration across a bucket's objects, and group-based bucket policies grant access without listing individual users. There is no documented general-purpose bulk or batch operation capability, so support is thin and inferred from these constructs. Missing for 10: an explicit bulk/batch API or console action across arbitrary items (e.g. multi-select delete or update), documented limits and semantics for bulk operations, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: A Node Pool in CKS represents one or more instances that share a common configuration, such as the same labels, taints, and annotations.
Bucket lifecycle policies is the reference for supported lifecycle actions (Expiration, NoncurrentVersionExpiration, AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload)
letting you grant or restrict access based on a principal's group memberships rather than listing individual users
